newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela crude reserves to 68 bln barrels in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela crude reserves to 68 bln barrels in 1997.

text.p: Venezuelan state-owned oil company PdVSA said Friday it planned to increase its crude reserves by 2.58 billion barrels in 1997 to 68.18 billion barrels.
The forecast appeared in a statement released by PdVSA after its annual general meeting.

PdVSA also said it approved investment plans of 3.1 trillion bolivars ($6.33 billion at the officially projected 1997 average exchange rate of 490 bolivars per dollar), after cutting 466 billion bolivars ($991 million) from the budget.
The budget was cut "in order to reduce inflationary pressures in the wider economy", PdVSA said, and follows an International Monetary Fund (IMF) recommendation earlier this month.
Most of the investment will go to exploration and production, PdVSA said, "in order to meet increased market demand".
Although petrochemical production is seen rising 301,000 tonnes to 4.54 million tonnes, PdVSA gave no figures in the document as to projected oil and products output.

However, according to PdVSA sources, production of crudes, products and gas is expected to rise some 500,000 tonnes in 1997 to 3.7 million barrels per day (bpd), with some 600,000 bpd of that figure accounted for by gas production.
PdVSA exported an estimated 3.03 million bpd of crudes and products in 1997, versus some 2.75 million bpd in 1995.
